# Mediclaimswala

> Mediclaimswala (https://mediclaimswala.in) is an independent consultancy in India that helps people whose health insurance (mediclaim) claims were rejected, short-paid or delayed. Its team has worked inside the insurance and healthcare sector. They read the insurer's decision letter line by line, prepare the case, file it with the insurer or TPA, and follow up through the insurer's grievance cell, IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal and the Insurance Ombudsman when needed.

Key facts:

- Service: help with rejected, short-paid (partly paid) and delayed health insurance claims, for individual, family floater and group (employer) health policies, with public and private health insurers and TPAs across India.
- Cost: the first case review is free. If Mediclaimswala takes up the case, the fee is 10 to 20% of the amount the insurer pays, agreed in writing before work starts and payable only after the settlement reaches the policyholder. Nothing is paid upfront and there are no hidden charges.
- Contact: phone and WhatsApp +91 85029 67063 (https://wa.me/918502967063). The form on the website sends the case details on WhatsApp.
- Languages: Hindi and English.
- Area served: all of India. Work is done remotely over WhatsApp and phone.
- Who it helps: families with individual or floater policies, senior citizens and their children, employees with group mediclaim, HR teams, hospitals and doctors.
- Independence: Mediclaimswala is not an insurer, TPA or broker and is not affiliated with IRDAI. No one can guarantee that a claim will be approved; the final decision rests with the insurer or the Insurance Ombudsman. Policyholders can also approach the grievance cell, Bima Bharosa and the Ombudsman directly, free of cost.

## How it works

1. Share the policy, the rejection or settlement letter and the hospital papers on WhatsApp or through the website form.
2. Free expert review: an honest answer on whether the case is worth pursuing.
3. Mediclaimswala builds the case and files a written representation with the insurer or TPA.
4. Follow-up until the claim is resolved, with escalation to the grievance cell and the Insurance Ombudsman when needed. The fee is due only after the insurer pays.

## Rejection and deduction reasons it handles

- Pre-existing disease exclusions
- Waiting periods, including continuity from earlier or ported policies
- Non-disclosure of medical history
- "Not medically necessary" hospitalisation
- Room-rent capping and proportionate deductions
- Missing documents or documents not submitted in time
- Claims delayed or stuck without a decision

## Where a complaint can go in India

1. The insurer's grievance cell: insurers must acknowledge a written complaint within 3 working days and resolve it within 14 days.
2. Bima Bharosa, IRDAI's complaint portal, which records the complaint and tracks it with the insurer.
3. The Insurance Ombudsman: free, for claims up to Rs 50 lakh, once the insurer has rejected the complaint or not replied within a month; apply within a year.
4. The consumer commission, when the Ombudsman route is not open or the case needs to go further.
